title: Phantom: interact with invisible beings
team: Myeongseong Kim, Junbeom Shin, Donghyeon Ko, Woohun Lee
summary: A media art installation inspired by nature's antifouling strategies.
Ultrasonic vibrations push away fine particles to reveal hidden patterns, turning surface hygiene into an interactive experience.

paragraph: Phantom is an interactive media art installation that uses ultrasonic vibrations to reveal hidden patterns on a surface.
Visitors interact with the installation by placing a pebble on the board.
The system uses calibrated ultrasonic vibrations to selectively push fine particles away from the surface, gradually revealing intricate patterns.
As the particles move, an invisible force becomes visible through the traces it leaves behind.
The project draws inspiration from the antifouling properties of cicada and dragonfly wings, whose nanoscale pillars help keep their surfaces clean.
Translating this biological principle into an ultrasonic system, Phantom investigates how waves might produce similar repulsive effects,
exploring a new approach to surface hygiene through biomimicry.
By turning the act of clearing a surface into an aesthetic experience, Phantom invites reflection on the relationship between hygiene, nature, and technology.
The work was featured in Nature Observation 2.0, an exhibition hosted by HMG from November 22 to December 2, 2021.
